title: Phased Heartbeat Drain & Transactional Evacuation for Hosted + Dedicated
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Context:
In the last two cross-region incidents we saw tenant requests routed into a degraded region where leader leases and KV snapshots lagged. That produced partial transactional failures for a subset of tenants on Dedicated pools and noisy error rates for Hosted customers behind those pools. This ticket creates a repeatable, tested runbook that prioritizes transactional consistency during evacuations by introducing a phased 'heartbeat drain' and explicit transactional quiesce before bulk traffic rehome. The playbook is intended for both Hosted and Dedicated routing planes and must be safe for hybrid customers using private VPC routing.

Goals:
- Avoid partial commit anomalies for transactional workloads during region moves.
- Minimize customer-facing errors and retries while keeping latency SLOs reasonable.
- Produce a clear on-call checklist, automated guardrail scripts, and an ops runbook with rollback and customer comms.

Playbook overview (high level):
1) Detection & Triage: confirm region degradation via E2E call traces, KV-applier-lag > 2s, and tenant error rates > 3x baseline. Notify SRE, ENG on-call, and PM for affected tenant list.
2) Quarantine & Gentle Drain (Heartbeat Drain): reduce routing weight to 30% for affected region and enable per-tenant sticky drain tokens. Keep a minimal heartbeat stream to allow KV & lease renewals. This prevents sudden leader churn.
3) Transactional Quiesce: for tenants with transactional guarantees, issue a graceful quiesce API that stops new writes (timeout 10s) and completes in-flight transactions. Snapshot latest transaction sequence numbers to storage for transfer.
4) Snapshot Transfer & Verify: copy KV transaction snapshots to target region, validate checksums and sequence continuity using the verification tool (audit-check v2).
5) Progressive Migration (Circuit Peeling): shift traffic in 10% increments from drained region to target region with 2 min observation windows; validate p50/p95 latency, error budget, and KV read-after-write consistency for a representative suite.
6) Promote & Cutover: when metrics stable for 3 observation windows, promote target region leaders for affected tenants, remove drain tokens, and restore normal routing weights via the routing-control service.
7) Postmortem & Customer Follow-up: capture incident timeline, PRs, and customer-impact summary; schedule follow-up patch to prevent recurrence.

Runbook artifacts & links:
- Internal runbook draft (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/heartbeat-drain-evac
- Verification tool (audit-check v2): https://github.com/redwood-inference/audit-check/pull/198
- Routing-control scripts prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing-control/compare/evac-guards
- Incident dashboard template: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/incident/evac-template
- Slack incident channel: #inc-evac-hosted-dedicated

Safety considerations / Rollback:
- At any progression stage if read-after-write anomalies are detected, immediately stop promotions, rollback routing weight to previous stable snapshot, and re-enable write quiesce until manual reconciliation completes.
- If KV snapshot checksum mismatches occur, pause migration and fall back to dual-write mode (short window) while we run leader reconciliation.

Testing & Rehearsal plan:
- Unit test suites for routing weight transitions and heartbeat drain logic (CI gate).
- Staging chaos test: runbook replay on staging with synthetic tenant workload including long-running transactions and leader lease flaps.
- Quarterly fire drills: 2 scheduled rehearsals per quarter with SRE, ENG, PM, and Solutions engineers and a customer success observer.

Open design trade-offs noted:
- Aggressive drain (0% immediate) reduces customer exposure but spikes leader election and inflight write failures; elected approach uses slow drain with heartbeat to protect leases.
- Dual-write fallback introduces complexity but may be necessary for a small set of high-throughput tenants; include guardrail timeouts and automated cutover checks.

Acceptance criteria:
- Automated script available to perform the phased drain end-to-end in under 10 minutes (excluding snapshot transfer).
- Playbook run in staging with no data consistency regressions across 5 rehearsal runs.
- Documentation and customer-communication templates published and reviewed by PM and Legal.
